audit.note: both validations run in the backend over the two bound fields

deviations.what: the Name input's binding carries a sap.ui.model.type.String with minLength 1 / maxLength 10 constraints, and UI5 checks those in the BROWSER on every parse. The port keeps the binding exactly as written (path plus type plus constraints, the app 549 composite-binding idiom) so that half still works client-side, and the backend checks the same two bounds when it is asked to.

the E-mail input's binding names '.customEMailType', a sap.ui.model.SimpleType the CONTROLLER defines, whose validateValue throws a ValidateException unless the value matches /^\w+[\w-+\.]*\@\w+([-\.]\w+)*\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$/. A model type is a JavaScript class - there is nothing to name from a backend - so the type reference is dropped and the same shape is checked in ABAP instead: exactly one @ with something before it, a dot in the domain with at least two characters after it, and no spaces. The sample's own comment calls its regex demonstration-only, so the two agree on every value it is meant to show.

_validateInput reads the binding's type, calls validateValue and sets the input's valueState to Error or None. valueState IS a bindable property, so the port binds one field per input and writes it from the same check. The two valueStateTexts are carried literally, as the sample writes them.

onInit registers both inputs with sap.ui.core.Messaging (registerObject), which is what makes UI5 attach its own validation-error handling and paint the state on a failed parse. There is no counterpart for the registration itself; what it produces - the Error state on an invalid value - the port writes explicitly.
onSubmit's two outcomes are carried 1:1: a MessageToast on success and MessageBox.alert on failure (message_box_display with the information type, which is what alert shows).
not yet verified in a running system: that a name over ten characters paints the Error state and that Submit distinguishes the two outcomes.
